methodologyNotes: Dataset covers 13 robot window cleaners spanning current flagship (Ecovacs WINBOT W3 Omni, W2S Omni), mainstream corded (HOBOT 2S/388/R3, Mamibot, Cop Rose, HUTT) and budget/niche (Alfawise, Gladwell, Sichler) tiers. Seed list corrections: 'Ecovacs Winbot X' (2018) is no longer listed on ecovacs.com/us/shop and has been dropped as discontinued; 'Ecovacs Winbot W2 Omni' is confirmed real but shows 'Sold out' on the current ecovacs.com US shop page, so it was replaced with its in-market successors, the WINBOT W3 Omni (CES 2026 flagship) and WINBOT W2S Omni (current mid-tier Omni model); Mamibot W120-T is a legacy (~2018) SKU no longer on mamibot.com's current lineup (which now leads with the W300/W120-DP/W120-P/W200 SkyBot) but is kept because it is still actively sold via Amazon/eBay and was an explicit seed — Mamibot W120-DP (2024, 3200Pa, 'thinnest robot window cleaner' per manufacturer) was added as the current-generation Mamibot expansion. Sichler PR-041 is a German/Austrian (PEARL/Sichler Haushaltsgeräte) private-label rebrand of HOBOT hardware (PR-041 V3 ≈ HOBOT-268 generation; the current-gen successor REF-60579 is explicitly a rebadged HOBOT-298) sold only in the DACH region — no US listing exists, so priceUsd is null by design, not by omission. suction_power_pa is left null for every HOBOT-family unit and for Mamibot W120-T, Gladwell Gecko and Cop Rose X6 where the manufacturer publishes suction only as kgf force or does not publish a figure at all (HOBOT rates 'ascending power' in kg, e.g. HOBOT-2S ≈ 6.0–7.0 kgf depending on region, HOBOT-R3 ≈ 5 kgf) — converting kgf to Pa would require assumptions about contact-cup area that were not published, so null was used rather than an estimate. battery_backup_min is the full untethered battery runtime for the dual-power Ecovacs Omni models (they can run entirely on battery) and the UPS/backup-only duration (keeps the unit clamped to the glass during a power or Wi-Fi/cable failure — NOT a cordless-use runtime) for every corded model (all HOBOT, Mamibot, Cop Rose, Alfawise, Sichler and HUTT units). Several small retailer/manufacturer storefronts (hobot.us, acevacuums.com, shop.prosperahealth.com, gladwellclean.com, robowindow.com — all Shopify-hosted) returned HTTP 429 bot-protection responses on every direct fetch attempt during verification, and Amazon.com product pages could not be rendered at all (consistent 500 errors); where this blocked confirmation of a live US price, priceUsd was left null with the conflicting/partial figures actually found (search-engine cache snippets of the real page, other regions, or older press coverage) documented in priceNote/provenance rather than guessed. Every image was independently fetched and visually confirmed to show the correct product (read back as a decoded image) before inclusion, except where noted 'omitted' in provenance because no verifiable direct image file could be found. accessedAt 2026-08-01 for all sources, corroborations and images unless individually noted.

products.name: Ecovacs WINBOT W3 Omni
products.priceNote: MSRP per ecovacs.com US shop page; unveiled at CES 2026 (Jan 6-9); frequently bundled/discounted to ~$594-654

specs.cleaning_speed_mode: 8 modes (Fast/Deep/Thorough/Edge/Spot/Zone/Heavy-duty/Remote); 16 cm/s top speed, ~1m35s per 1x1m panel in Fast mode
specs.spray_system: 3-nozzle wide-angle spray, 80ml tank, >=70% spray coverage; Vortex Wash station auto-washes pads with 16 jets (~1 min cycle)
specs.safety_tether: 3-layer composite power/safety cable rated to 100kg, plus 1m backup rope
specs.edge_detection: Optocoupler edge sensor, 0.02s response; TruEdge retracting scrubber cleans to ~1.1cm of the frame

products.provenance: Fetched live from ecovacs.com/us: $699.99 price, 10,000Pa headline suction (page separately lists a 3300±100Pa figure for the robot while moving — both are genuine manufacturer figures, headline used here), 80ml/3-nozzle spray, WIN-SLAM 5.0, 100kg-rated composite tether, 0.02s optocoupler edge sensor, 130-minute dual-power battery mode. Robot-only weight (4.9 lb) and 71.5dB noise level are not on the manufacturer page (which only gives packaged 12.22kg and station 10kg) and were corroborated via search-engine aggregation of retailer listings and a Galaxus.at measured review. Gizmodo's hands-on review (fetched live) independently confirms the $700 price and 130-minute runtime. Release: CES 2026 debut per ECOVACS PR Newswire coverage. Image is Ecovacs' own official product photo, fetched and visually confirmed to show the WINBOT W3 Omni robot with its Vortex Wash station.
